correctness.rationale: The exact laws follow by maximality/private leaves and independent priority-triple/last-job events, with all boundary cases \(m\ge1\) identified. The standalone stdlib-only verify.py uses inductively exhaustive leaf-extension generation with a canonical center encoding, exact rational recurrences, and both bipartition orientations. On 1974 orientations through 12 vertices none has edge advantage; among 2602 thirteen-vertex orientations exactly one, the four-arm spider, has edge-minus-vertex expected size 1/6480. The checker ran successfully from its actual package path; analytic formulas were compared with independent finite DP cases up to \(m=6\), and tree isomorphism counts were independently compared with a second generator. Finite checks prove only the finite cutoff; arbitrary m is proved analytically. Direct priority-permutation enumeration independently checks all 9! edge orders at three arms and all 46,080 job/local-neighbor priority profiles at four arms.

value.rationale: The sharp tree threshold answers a motivated question left by averaging theorems: graph-wise dominance can fail even on highly symmetric trees. The closed pair of failure probabilities exposes a nontrivial structural mechanism and proves infinitely many strict stochastic-order reversals, rather than reporting a single numerical anomaly. The complete smallest-order and unique-exception census is a natural boundary test; its exact value and structural explanation are useful independently of a stronger classification of all trees.
